title: Internal-Hom comparison respects the finite stratification triangles
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $g:X'\to X$ a morphism of schemes and $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], derived tensor $\otimes_A^L$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], and derived internal Hom $\mathscr H_T(U,V)=R\mathcal Hom_{A_T}(U,V)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Scheme inverse images on these categories are exact constant-coefficient inverse images [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. For every $K$ let $\beta_{K,M}:g^*\mathscr H_X(K,M)\to\mathscr H_{X'}(g^*K,g^*M)$ be the transpose of pulled-back evaluation under the canonical derived tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For every distinguished triangle $K'\to K\to K''\to K'[1]$ [def-weil-triangulated-category], the three maps $\beta_{K'',M},\beta_{K,M},\beta_{K',M}$, and the shift of $\beta_{K'',M}$ form a morphism between the distinguished triangles
$$g^*\mathscr H_X(K'',M)\to g^*\mathscr H_X(K,M)\to g^*\mathscr H_X(K',M)\to g^*\mathscr H_X(K'',M)[1]$$
and
$$\mathscr H_{X'}(g^*K'',g^*M)\to\mathscr H_{X'}(g^*K,g^*M)\to\mathscr H_{X'}(g^*K',g^*M)\to\mathscr H_{X'}(g^*K'',g^*M)[1],$$
using the canonical cochain shift and sign conventions. In particular, if two of the three comparison maps are isomorphisms, so is the third.

proof.text: Put $F=g^*$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], $F$ is exact on ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves. Consequently its termwise derived functor preserves distinguished triangles and commutes with cochain shifts by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Apply [lem-sf-hom-triangulated] first on $X$ and then on $X'$ to the given triangle and its $F$-image. Its first-variable clause gives exactly the two reversed Hom triangles in the statement, the first followed by $F$. These results are unbounded and require neither constructibility nor invertibility of the coefficient order.

proof.text:
Fix a complex representing $M$ and a K-injective representative $I$ for it; take a K-injective resolution $q:FI\to J$ on $X'$ [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Thus $J$ represents $FM$, since $F$ is exact. For a complex $E$ representing $K$, [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] gives $H(E,I)$ representing $\mathscr H_X(K,M)$ and $H'(FE,J)$ representing $\mathscr H_{X'}(FK,FM)$. Using [lem-sf-etale-hom-complex-pullback], form
$$b_E:H_F=F H(E,I)\xrightarrow{c_{E,I}}H'(FE,FI)\xrightarrow{H'(1,q)}H'(FE,J).$$
This is a chain map, natural contravariantly in $E$. Its first term computes $F\mathscr H_X(K,M)$ by exactness of $F$. No claim that $FI$ is K-injective is made: the last arrow uses the actual resolution $q$.

source.place: Tags 08J7 (section-internal-hom), 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom) and 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated); agent evaluation and signed-shift comparison argument.

proof.text: Identify $Qb_E$ with $\beta_{K,M}$ by its evaluation, rather than choosing an isomorphism of Hom objects. First choose $E$ K-flat with flat terms and choose a K-flat resolution $P\to H(E,I)$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The pullbacks $FE,FP$ remain K-flat, and the canonical tensor comparison is computed on these representatives [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback, lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. On each bidegree $(n,p)$ the tensor transpose of $b_E$ is precisely $q^{p+n}\circ F(\mathrm{ev}_{n,p})$, by the defining component formula of [lem-sf-etale-hom-complex-pullback]. After precomposing with $FP\otimes FE$, this is the pullback of the ordinary Hom evaluation followed by $q$. Hence it represents $F(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})$ under the derived tensor comparison. The tensor-Hom bijection and its evaluation formula [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] make its transpose unique, so $Qb_E=\beta_{K,M}$. For arbitrary $E$, replace it by a K-flat resolution: naturality of $b_E$, exactness of $F$, and the quasi-isomorphism invariance of Hom into K-injectives [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] give the same identity. Here $Q$ denotes localization to the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tags 08J7 (section-internal-hom), 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom) and 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated); agent evaluation and signed-shift comparison argument.

proof.text: The chain maps $b_E$ commute with precomposition in every chain map $E\to E'$ by the naturality clause of [lem-sf-etale-hom-complex-pullback] and componentwise Hom functoriality [def-pur-hom-complex]. Their source and target functors invert quasi-isomorphisms by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and exactness of $F$. Thus their naturality squares descend to every derived morphism: they commute with localized chain maps and with inverses of localized quasi-isomorphisms, hence with their composites. By step 3 this is naturality of the actual $\beta$ in its contravariant variable.

source.place: Tags 08J7 (section-internal-hom), 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom) and 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated); agent evaluation and signed-shift comparison argument.

proof.text: Keep the same $I,J,q$ for $E$ and $E[m]$. The shift square for $c$ is the last equality of [lem-sf-etale-hom-complex-pullback]. Postcomposition with $q$ respects the source-shift maps as well: in degree $n$ its $p$-component on both paths is $(-1)^{mn}q^{p+n-m}f^{p-m}$, by [def-pur-hom-complex]. Therefore $b_{E[m]}$ identifies with $b_E[-m]$ under the signed source-shift maps. By steps 2--3 and the signed shift identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], this descends to $\beta_{K[m],M}=\beta_{K,M}[-m]$ under those identifications. The termwise $F$ commutes with shifts by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. This verifies the required shift square including its signs, without using preservation of infinite products.

source.place: Tags 08J7 (section-internal-hom), 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom) and 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated); agent evaluation and signed-shift comparison argument.

proof.text: Write the input arrows as $u:K'\to K$, $v:K\to K''$ and $w:K''\to K'[1]$. Naturality from step 4 at $v$ and $u$ gives the first two comparison squares between the reversed triangles. For the boundary, use naturality at the shifted arrow $w[-1]:K''[-1]\to K'$ and the shift identity of step 5 to replace the component at $K''[-1]$ by $\beta_{K'',M}[1]$. The last-arrow sign in the reversed triangle is the same on both rows by [lem-sf-hom-triangulated]; multiplying the naturality equality by that common sign gives exactly the third square. Thus the three specified maps, with the specified shifted first component, form a morphism of the two distinguished triangles. Apply [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] to this morphism: any two invertible components force the third to be invertible.
